source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Heater and Air Conditioning, p.1A-35

procedures.title: Compressor oil charge: check
steps: If installing a field-repaired compressor, put in 1 extra fluid oz. of oil.
If the compressor cannot be idled first (step 1) to bring oil back into it, take it off, drain the oil, measure it and throw it away.
If more than 1-1/2 fluid oz. came out and there is no sign of a major leak, put that same amount into the replacement compressor.
If less than 1-1/2 fluid oz. came out and the system seems to have lost a lot of oil, put 6 fluid oz. of clean refrigeration oil into a replacement compressor, or 7 fluid oz. into a repaired one.
If the drained oil has chips or other debris, replace the receiver-dehydrator, flush or replace parts as needed, and add the full specified oil volume to the system.
For any other parts being replaced, add oil: evaporator 3 fluid oz., condenser 1 fluid oz., receiver-dehydrator 1 fluid oz.

specs.what: oil for replacement compressor (low drain, excessive loss)
oil for repaired compressor (low drain, excessive loss)

notes: When pouring oil into the compressor, raise its rear end so oil does not escape from the suction and discharge ports; never stand the compressor on its shaft end.

procedures.title: Refrigeration oil: add to the system
steps: Have the system fully assembled and with no refrigerant charge before adding oil.
Hook the charging station low pressure gauge line to the low pressure gauge fitting on the POA valve (Four-Season and Comfortron systems).
Hook the charging station high pressure line to the compressor muffler (or the high side of the connector block).
Disconnect the high pressure line at the gauge set, check it is clean, and set its end in a graduated container.
Pour enough refrigeration oil in the container for the required volume to be pulled into the system through the high pressure hose.
Close the gauge set high pressure valve and open the low pressure valve.
Run the vacuum pump to lower system pressure so atmospheric pressure pushes oil up the high pressure line.
Once the oil level has dropped by the required amount, lift the line out of the container and keep pumping to clear the oil in the line into the system.
Stop the vacuum pump and reconnect the high pressure line to the gauge set.
Open the high pressure valve and evacuate through both high and low sides.
Finish charging as in step 6 of Evacuating and Charging System.
notes: Use only clean Frigidaire 525 viscosity refrigeration oil.

procedures.title: A/C component replacement: preparing the system
steps: Read the earlier parts of this section before servicing.
Keep the work area clean and plug or cap every opened component and hose.
When a repair opens the refrigerant circuit, first purge the system by venting the refrigerant to atmosphere.
Remove and replace the faulty part.
Evacuate the system and charge it with R-12.
notes: Component procedures are grouped as All Systems, Four-Season and Comfortron, then Four-Season only, Comfortron only and GM Chevrolet Air Conditioner only.
Caution: wear protective goggles (J-5453, part of the A/C special tool set) on refrigeration work, and do not run the engine in a closed or poorly ventilated garage (carbon monoxide).
Any foreign material found in the system must be cleaned out before the system is put back in service.
